raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

Enable decoder SWA bounded replay by default for supported standalone CUDA DeepSeek-V4.1 configurations, while preserving an explicit full-prefill opt-out. In our paired accuracy runs, AIME 2026 without an explicit output cap was identical (469/480 each); DeepSWE differed by one solved task and MMMU-Pro by five correct responses. These are finite, stochastic accuracy measurements, not proof of numerical equivalence or a universal speedup.

## Modifications

- Enable decoder replay by default on CUDA DSv4.1 unless `disable_decoder_bounded_replay` is set for eager/breakable prefill, with the existing DP-attention compatibility checks. Keep PD, context parallelism, encoder replay, other platforms, and incompatible configurations out of automatic enablement.
- Preserve explicit `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`; add `--disable-decoder-bounded-replay` to retain full prefill, including prompt-logprob support. Bounded replay remains numerically different from full prefill and does not support prompt logprobs.
- Include the candidate-table capacity fix needed for speculative verification beyond the 1,048,576-token boundary. Select the existing 16 KiB or expanded 32 KiB bitmap according to page-table capacity; reject unsupported capacities above 2M tokens. This fixes a shared indexer issue, not a replay-only failure, and does not enlarge the model context limit.
- Add default-resolution/CLI coverage and eager/CUDA-graph sorter boundary regressions; update the model cookbook and CLI help.

Base: upstream main `9d68ecce2e811d908551d58a2a8792c75245d181`. Main already includes breakable-prefill replay support; this PR does not reapply the historical #43440 patch wholesale.

## Accuracy Tests

### Completed benchmark results

Each arm used one 4×GB300 node and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, checkpoint `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`. Replay off/on was the intended server-setting difference. TP=4, EP=4, attention DP=1, DSPARK block size=5, FlashMLA, static memory fraction=0.8, max running requests=64, decode graph max batch=64, breakable prefill max tokens=4096, prefill graph max sequence length=16384, chunked prefill=16384, and server random seed=0 were shared.

| Workload | Samples per arm | Replay off | Replay on | Truncations off / on | Harness/request errors off / on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSWE | 113 tasks, one attempt | 78/113 = 69.03% resolved | 77/113 = 68.14% resolved | Not aggregated by this harness | 0 / 0 |
| AIME 2026, initial 32,768-token cap | 30 questions × 16 = 480 | 453/480 = 94.38% | 447/480 = 93.13% | 25 / 31 | 0 / 0 |
| AIME 2026, no explicit output cap | 30 questions × 16 = 480 | 469/480 = 97.71% | 469/480 = 97.71% | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| MMMU-Pro standard (10 options), repaired runs | 1,730 questions × 1 | 1,152/1,730 = 66.59% | 1,147/1,730 = 66.30% | 18 / 28 | 0 / 0 |

AIME majority@16 was 96.67% for both capped runs and 100% for both uncapped runs. The capped results are included for completeness; the uncapped rerun removes the artificial 32K cutoff. Its largest observed outputs were 120,168 tokens off and 107,673 on.

DeepSWE used deep-swe `0b9fabbb63b9104d678fe965e1632f2dd9eaa2ea`, Pier `4d3c14041d16443f3f9f460dcdf23629994a304e`, mini-swe-agent 2.4.6, Docker task environments, four concurrent trials per arm, temperature=1, top_p=.95, max_tokens=32768, seed=0, and reasoning effort high. No sgl-eval changes were involved in that agent harness.

AIME/MMMU used unmodified sgl-eval 0.1.2 at `93bc2d851a59e57d54fe755202756589a04d3d86`: concurrency=16, temperature=1, top_p=.95, thinking enabled, reasoning effort high, no per-request seed. MMMU used the existing image loader, prompt and MCQ grader for `MMMU/MMMU_Pro`, configuration `standard (10 options)`, test split. This is `mmmu_pro`, not `mmmu_pro_vision` or `mmlu_pro`.

Example full MMMU command (use separate output directories and endpoints per arm):

```bash
sgl-eval run mmmu_pro \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:31000/v1 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --n-repeats 1 --num-threads 16 \
  --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 \
  --thinking --reasoning-effort high \
  --out-dir results
```

A one-image smoke evaluation (`--num-examples 1`) passed on each arm before the full run. Full MMMU artifacts were checked for 1,730 distinct matching IDs, matching question text/expected answers and generation settings, zero exit codes, and recomputed accuracy/finish-reason counts. Saved server configurations differ only in replay selection after excluding runtime metadata. The installed repaired kernel hashes match. The loader did not pin the Hugging Face dataset revision; final prediction files do not contain image bytes for independent byte equality checks.

### Revision scope and the original MMMU failure

These full benchmark runs predate the PR base above. DeepSWE/AIME ran on main `b60444c62169c7992b98f102cbc4e86d9d117294` plus #43440 head `729c1584e597c915f6dbb6207b89e90a09fcef33`, integrated locally as `b273c67e75a70c1971eb7715910d15c148136883`. Repaired MMMU added local fix `6dc4fa29df069c92668de2fc5ed7766dd49e378b`, transplanted in this PR. The full benchmarks have not been rerun on the new main/default-selection patch.

Both original MMMU arms crashed at the context boundary with `logical_page_idx < block_table_stride`. A minimal sorter reproducer passed at 1M tokens but lost the newest candidate at 1M+1, returning `INT32_MAX`. Original interrupted scores are invalid and excluded from the accuracy table. Both arms were rerun fresh with the same fix; both completed without request errors.

Omitting max_tokens still permits context-limit truncation. Repaired MMMU reached maximum generated lengths of 1,048,271 off and 1,048,285 on. The remaining truncations reflect length stopping, not a recurrence of the server crash.

Historical fix validation also included six sparse-indexer tests, sorter boundaries at 1,048,575 / 1,048,576 / 1,048,577 / 1,048,586 / 2,097,152 tokens in eager and captured execution, and an end-to-end DSPARK request with 1,048,544 input tokens plus 30 output tokens followed by a healthy server. The text-only boundary reproducer shows that images are not necessary to trigger this bug.

### Validation on the new PR base

- Seven default-resolution and CLI tests passed against the updated source on a GB300 node, including the disable flag and conflicting-flag rejection.
- The candidate boundary regression passed: five lengths × eager/captured execution (ten subcases).
- Six existing sparse-prefill indexer tests passed against the new source on GB300.
- Scoped pre-commit checks passed, including formatting, AST checks, and registered-test validation.

These ran in isolated test processes with the new source; the benchmark servers were not restarted. Full workload reruns, a complete documentation-site build, and upstream CI are not claimed here. Recommended CI covers the new server-argument test, encoder/decoder replay row tests, candidate boundary and sparse-indexer tests, and the GB300 DSv4.1 E2E. The current B300 PD+CP E2E is disabled upstream.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Workload | Replay off evaluation time | Replay on evaluation time |
|---|---:|---:|
| AIME 2026, 32K cap | 876.22 s | 869.16 s |
| AIME 2026, no explicit cap | 1,064.43 s | 1,037.55 s |
| MMMU-Pro, repaired | 7,291.75 s | 8,635.92 s |

DeepSWE took approximately 6h 5m per arm, including agent tool execution and task grading. These are end-to-end workload durations, not isolated prefill latency measurements.

MMMU generated 31,363,333 completion tokens off versus 42,100,497 on. Aggregate output rates were 4,301 versus 4,875 tokens/s, but different output lengths, reasoning loops, and batch occupancy prevent treating that ratio as a controlled replay speedup. The controlled fixed-token comparison below measures speed separately from these accuracy workloads. Single stochastic runs also do not establish statistical equivalence of accuracy.

Recorded runtime: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sgl-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer/cubin 0.7.1, FlashInfer JIT cache 0.7.1+cu130; Python UnifiedTreeCore fallback on both arms.

### Controlled fixed-token comparison on 4×GB300

Measured October 16, 2026 on the same node, sequentially replay off then on. Identical deterministic synthetic token-ID prompts, temperature=0, `ignore_eos=true`, exact output lengths, and three repetitions per case. Shape-specific warmup and server startup are excluded; the radix cache was flushed before each repetition. All 348 measured requests per arm passed exact prompt/output-length checks with zero cached tokens.

Both arms used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP4, attention DP=1, FlashMLA, DSPARK block size 5, breakable prefill, 16,384-token chunks, and a 16,384-token prefill graph context limit. Encoder replay was disabled. Effective server settings matched apart from decoder replay and runtime metadata.

**Single-request time to first token**, with one output token and five requests per repetition. Values are medians of the three per-repetition medians; speedup = off/on. This is client-observed first-token latency, not GPU-kernel-only time.

| Input tokens | Replay off TTFT | Replay on TTFT | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 42.89 ms | 42.92 ms | 0.999× |
| 8,192 | 174.50 ms | 172.54 ms | 1.011× |
| 32,768 | 480.92 ms | 346.89 ms | 1.386× |
| 65,536 | 974.77 ms | 700.62 ms | 1.391× |

**End-to-end output throughput**, with concurrency 16, 32 requests per repetition, and exactly 128 output tokens per request. Values are median repetition throughput; speedup = on/off.

| Input tokens | Replay off output tokens/s | Replay on output tokens/s | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 2054.97 | 2107.11 | 1.025× |
| 8,192 | 792.69 | 885.98 | 1.118× |
| 32,768 | 256.38 | 337.22 | 1.315× |

Long-prompt first-token latency improved by approximately **1.39× (28% lower latency)** at 32K/64K input; 32K concurrent throughput improved **1.315×**. Short single-request latency was essentially unchanged. Concurrent TTFT did not improve uniformly: at 1K input it was 163 ms off versus 184 ms on.

**Revision and interpretation limits:** these measurements use the retained repaired accuracy-test runtime, not a fresh checkout of current main or this PR head. The installed package reports `0.0.0.dev1+g67eab5705`; that build-version string alone does not identify later local patches. The candidate-table header SHA-256 matches the repaired benchmark (`d7088c2ac6c282ef2ae42cadcf527b21c36b165501add4d449b1c596bbbd16a2`). Synthetic token IDs control input shape but do not represent natural-language quality or every production workload. DSPARK acceptance can differ between modes even with fixed output counts. The sequential order was not counterbalanced, and three repetitions do not establish statistical confidence.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add default-selection, CLI, and candidate-boundary tests.
- [x] Document default scope and opt-out.
- [x] Provide accuracy results and workload timings with revision and interpretation limits.

Aggregate output rates were 4,301 versus 4,875 tokens/s, but different output lengths, reasoning loops, and batch occupancy prevent treating that ratio as a controlled replay speedup. The controlled fixed-token comparison below measures speed separately from these accuracy workloads. Single stochastic runs also do not establish statistical equivalence of accuracy.

Recorded runtime: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sgl-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer/cubin 0.7.1, FlashInfer JIT cache 0.7.1+cu130; Python UnifiedTreeCore fallback on both arms.

### Controlled fixed-token comparison on 4×GB300

Measured October 16, 2026 on the same node, sequentially replay off then on. Identical deterministic synthetic token-ID prompts, temperature=0, `ignore_eos=true`, exact output lengths, and three repetitions per case. Shape-specific warmup and server startup are excluded; the radix cache was flushed before each repetition. All 348 measured requests per arm passed exact prompt/output-length checks with zero cached tokens.

Both arms used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP4, attention DP=1, FlashMLA, DSPARK block size 5, breakable prefill, 16,384-token chunks, and a 16,384-token prefill graph context limit. Encoder replay was disabled. Effective server settings matched apart from decoder replay and runtime metadata.

**Single-request time to first token**, with one output token and five requests per repetition. Values are medians of the three per-repetition medians; speedup = off/on. This is client-observed first-token latency, not GPU-kernel-only time.

| Input tokens | Replay off TTFT | Replay on TTFT | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 42.89 ms | 42.92 ms | 0.999× |
| 8,192 | 174.50 ms | 172.54 ms | 1.011× |
| 32,768 | 480.92 ms | 346.89 ms | 1.386× |
| 65,536 | 974.77 ms | 700.62 ms | 1.391× |

**End-to-end output throughput**, with concurrency 16, 32 requests per repetition, and exactly 128 output tokens per request. Values are median repetition throughput; speedup = on/off.

| Input tokens | Replay off output tokens/s | Replay on output tokens/s | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 2054.97 | 2107.11 | 1.025× |
| 8,192 | 792.69 | 885.98 | 1.118× |
| 32,768 | 256.38 | 337.22 | 1.315× |

Long-prompt first-token latency improved by approximately **1.39× (28% lower latency)** at 32K/64K input; 32K concurrent throughput improved **1.315×**. Short single-request latency was essentially unchanged. Concurrent TTFT did not improve uniformly: at 1K input it was 163 ms off versus 184 ms on.

**Revision and interpretation limits:** these measurements use the retained repaired accuracy-test runtime, not a fresh checkout of current main or this PR head. The installed package reports `0.0.0.dev1+g67eab5705`; that build-version string alone does not identify later local patches. The candidate-table header SHA-256 matches the repaired benchmark (`d7088c2ac6c282ef2ae42cadcf527b21c36b165501add4d449b1c596bbbd16a2`). Synthetic token IDs control input shape but do not represent natural-language quality or every production workload. DSPARK acceptance can differ between modes even with fixed output counts. The sequential order was not counterbalanced, and three repetitions do not establish statistical confidence.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add default-selection, CLI, and candidate-boundary tests.
- [x] Document default scope and opt-out.
- [x] Provide accuracy results and workload timings with revision and interpretation limits.

@@ -105,7 +105,7 @@ import { agentx } from "/src/snippets/agentx/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4_1.jsx";
 
 **Engram.** An additive n-gram hash memory at two layers. Token ids are normalized *before* hashing, so `" The"`, `"the"` and `"THE"` cannot fork into separate rows. Its two fp8 tables are the largest single block of weight in the checkpoint, and by default they load row-sharded across the TP group, which costs an all-reduce per engram layer. `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1` (**opt-in**) moves them to host memory instead: the freed HBM goes to the KV pool and output is bitwise unchanged — at the cost of host RAM, a longer load, and needing huge-page backing to keep the gather cheap. `SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT` trades the two all-reduces for page size: `shared` (the default) maps a single copy all ranks read and needs no reduce; `per_rank` splits that same table into one shard per rank and keeps the reduce, but is the only one the kernel reliably backs with 2 MiB pages.
 
-**SWA bounded replay.** Because the window store is per-layer and cheap to rebuild, it need not all be recomputed. `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` (**opt-in**) runs the early layers over the whole extend and the late layers over only each request's last 128 tokens, sharing late-layer KV from source layer 20. Prefill gets materially faster. It is validated on the decode path only, refuses prompt logprobs by design, is not numerically equivalent to full prefill, and is excluded at launch with the prefill CUDA graph and with DP attention. The one DP exception is ROCm with TP MoE and `--attn-dp-size` equal to `--tp` (see §3.6).
+**SWA bounded replay.** Decoder SWA bounded replay runs the early layers over the whole extend and the late layers over only each request’s last 128 tokens, sharing late-layer KV from source layer 20. It defaults on for supported standalone CUDA/HIP configurations without context parallelism. Encoder SWA replay can be combined with decoder replay, subject to encoder-specific validation. Eager and breakable prefill are supported; full prefill graphs keep it disabled. With DP attention, automatic enablement requires attention TP 1 and the `none` or `megamoe` MoE backend on CUDA, or `none` on HIP. Use `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` to explicitly enable replay, subject to compatibility validation. Use `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` to retain full prefill or request prompt logprobs. Bounded replay is not numerically equivalent to full prefill and does not support prompt logprobs.
 
 **Kernels.** At decode token counts these kernels are launch-bound rather than bandwidth-bound, so the work is fusion and overlap: the compressor projection, ratio-2 pooling, RoPE with fp4 quantization and indexer packing, paged fp4 indexer scoring with top-k resolved straight to cache addresses, and the mHC statistics and Sinkhorn — with compression, indexing and mHC overlapped against attention and FFN on dedicated streams. All of it is selected automatically; the environment switches it once sat behind were removed, so there is nothing to turn on. One caveat outranks the fusions: **output is not bitwise stable across batch composition today** — two default kernels are shape-guarded to a single token — and `--enable-deterministic-inference` is refused on this backend.

+"""Candidate tables must cover speculative rows beyond the 1M context boundary."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.candidate_table import (
+    build_sparse_indexer_schedule,
+    sort_candidate_blocks,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+
+class TestCandidateTableBoundary(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_speculative_context_boundary(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        page_size = 128
+        topk = 2048
+        for length in (1048575, 1048576, 1048577, 1048586, 2097152):
+            for captured in (False, True):
+                with self.subTest(length=length, captured=captured):
+                    nblocks = (length + 7) // 8
+                    chosen = torch.randperm(nblocks - 1, device="cuda")[: topk - 1]
+                    chosen = torch.cat([chosen, chosen.new_tensor([nblocks - 1])])
+                    blocks = chosen.to(torch.int32)[None, :].contiguous()
+                    expected = blocks.sort(dim=1).values
+                    lengths = torch.tensor([length], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+                    pages = torch.randperm((length + 127) // 128, device="cuda")
+                    pages = pages.to(torch.int32)[None, :].contiguous()
+                    request_ids = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+                    physical = torch.empty_like(blocks)
+                    # Warm up JIT before capturing; sorting is idempotent.
+                    sort_candidate_blocks(
+                        blocks, lengths, pages, page_size, out_pages=physical
+                    )
+                    build_sparse_indexer_schedule(
+                        blocks, lengths, pages, page_size, torch.int8, request_ids
+                    )
+                    if captured:
+                        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                            sort_candidate_blocks(
+                                blocks, lengths, pages, page_size, out_pages=physical
+                            )
+                        graph.replay()
+                    build_sparse_indexer_schedule(
+                        blocks, lengths, pages, page_size, torch.int8, request_ids
+                    )
+                    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(blocks, expected)
+                    expected_physical = (
+                        pages.gather(1, expected.long() // 16) * 16 + expected % 16
+                    )
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(physical, expected_physical)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
